To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the self is defined in relation to other people in the environment and that these relational self-construal can have profound effects on cognition, emotion, motivation, and behavior.
the construal of the independent self as a unique, autonomous entity is a cultural universal.
the self is construed differently in different cultures and these different construals have specific consequences for cognition, emotion, and motivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people think about and understand themselves in relation to other people and how such construals of self can have profound effects on cognition, emotion, emotion regulation, and motivation.
how culture affects the very nature of human experience.
the role of culture in the most fundamental aspects of individual experience, the role of culture as the most basic level of analysis in the study of individual experience.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
culture and self-construal are the most important variables in understanding the nature of individual experience.
the self is not a culture-free entity, but rather that it is a culture-dependent one.
the self-construal is a fundamental determinant of human experience, and that it varies dramatically among individuals and across cultures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the way in which the self is construed in a culture has profound implications for how people think, feel, and act.
the self is a fundamental aspect of human cognition, emotion, motivation, and behavior, and that the self is not only a universal, but a universal with many different forms.
the self is not just an individual's representation of his/her personal attributes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

people from different cultural backgrounds have strikingly different conceptions of the self, and that these conceptions have profound consequences for the very nature of their cognition, emotion, motivation, and behavior.
the self-construal of a person is a powerful determinant of the person's experience of the world.
culture is not a peripheral, trivial, and uninteresting variable in the study of the mind.
